Exact conditional Poisson regression (multivariate-shift algorithm)

Source: R/ep-multivariate-shift.R
ep_multi_shift.Rd

Exact conditional inference for one or more categorical effects in a Poisson regression with a log link, an optional offset, and optional stratification. Nuisance parameters (stratum intercepts and every model effect not listed in exact_vars) are eliminated by conditioning on their sufficient statistics, and the resulting exact conditional distribution of each requested effect's sufficient statistic is obtained by the multivariate-shift algorithm: a per-stratum dynamic program combined with explicit cross-stratum convolution, generalizing the multivariate shift algorithm of Hirji, Mehta, and Patel (1987) for exact logistic regression to bounded Poisson counts, following the EXACTMAX/OFFSET rules documented for SAS PROC GENMOD's EXACT statement.

Usage

ep_multi_shift(
  formula,
  data,
  exact_vars,
  offset = NULL,
  offset_log = TRUE,
  exactmax = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  ref_levels = list(),
  alpha = 0.05,
  ci_type = c("two-sided", "one-sided"),
  chunk_size = 4000L,
  condition_on = c("model", "exact"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula.

data

A data frame.

exact_vars

Character vector of model terms to compute exact results for. Each entry must name a term that appears in formula, exactly as SAS's EXACT statement requires. An entry can be a main effect ("region") or an interaction of any order, named by joining every variable in it with * or : ("region:gender" and "region*gender" both work, and the variables may be listed in either order). Interaction columns are matched via the model's own terms()/assign structure, not by name-guessing, so a term is never confused with a different term that happens to share a text prefix (e.g. requesting "region" in a model that also contains region:gender selects only region's own main-effect columns). Requesting a term does not automatically request any other term built from the same variable(s): a main effect and its interactions are entirely independent entries, so testing region while leaving region:gender untested keeps the interaction as an ordinary nuisance covariate (conditioned on under condition_on = "model", never tested); to test the interaction itself, add it as its own entry, e.g. exact_vars = c("region", "region:gender").

offset

Name of an offset variable in data, or NULL (default). If NULL, every observation is treated as contributing one unit of exposure (offset = 0 on the log scale).

offset_log

If TRUE (default), offset already holds log(exposure); if FALSE, it holds raw exposure.

exactmax

NULL (not specified), TRUE (specified without a variable), or a character variable name (SAS EXACTMAX=).

strata

Optional character vector of stratification variable names in data.

ref_levels

Optional named list of reference levels for categorical variables.

alpha

Significance level for confidence intervals.

ci_type

"two-sided" (default) or "one-sided", matching ep_closed_form()'s argument of the same name. For "one-sided", only the confidence limit on the informative side is computed for each parameter (the other is left at its boundary, -Inf or Inf); which side is informative is determined per parameter from the two one-sided tail probabilities at the null (see two_sided_from_tails()'s direction), exactly as in ep_closed_form().

chunk_size

Maximum number of rows processed at once while combining two strata's coefficient tables. Combining strata requires pairing every row of one stratum's table with every row of the other's; chunk_size bounds how many such pairs are materialized simultaneously, trading memory for speed. The default is generous for typical problems; lower it if combining strata runs out of memory, or raise it if memory is plentiful and speed matters more.

condition_on

"model" (default; condition on every other model effect, matching SAS) or "exact" (condition only on the other requested exact_vars).

verbose

If TRUE (default), prints progress and which SAS rule determined the per-observation caps.

Value

An object of class c("ep_multi_shift", "ep_fit"): a list with elements exactparmest (a one-row data frame with Parameter, Estimate (the coefficient beta = log rate ratio, not the rate ratio), StdError, Alpha, LowerCL, UpperCL (beta scale), PValue, and SuffStat), OUTDIST (the exact distribution of the sufficient statistic), and call.

Details

formula may contain interaction terms (a*b, a:b, or higher-order interactions) freely, in two distinct roles. An interaction can be a plain adjustment covariate, left out of exact_vars entirely, in which case it is conditioned on like any other nuisance term (under the default condition_on = "model") but never itself tested. Or an interaction can be the effect of interest, including an interaction of the effect of interest with another covariate, by listing it as its own entry in exact_vars; see that argument's documentation for the exact naming rules. The two roles are independent: listing a main effect in exact_vars never implicitly tests its interactions, and listing an interaction never implicitly tests the main effects it is built from, each term to be tested must be named explicitly.

References

Hirji KF, Mehta CR, Patel NR. Computing Distributions for Exact Logistic Regression. JASA, 82(400):1110-1117, 1987.

Mehta CR, Patel NR. Exact logistic regression: theory and examples. Statistics in Medicine, 14(19):2143-2160, 1995.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  group = c( 1L,  1L,  1L,  0L,  0L,  0L),
  age      = c(50L, 60L, 70L, 50L, 60L, 70L),
  subjects = c(3492, 2141, 1711, 3525, 2166, 1724),
  cases    = c(   3,    2,    1,   10,   7,   5),
  futime   = c(50, 60, 40, 51, 62, 42)
)

df$lnfutime <- log(df$futime)

ep_multi_shift(
  formula    = cases ~ group,
  data       = df,
  offset     = "lnfutime",
  offset_log = TRUE,
  strata     = "age",
  exact_vars = "group",
  ref_levels = list(group="0", age="50"),
  alpha      = 0.05,
  verbose    = TRUE,
  ci_type = "two-sided"
)
#> 
#> SAS rule (3): OFFSET specified and EXACTMAX not specified =>
#>                 S_i = max(ceil(exp(o_i)),1).
#> 
#> === EXACT for parameter column: group1 ===
#>   stratum 50: n=2, M=13
#>   stratum 60: n=2, M=9
#>   stratum 70: n=2, M=6
#>   after combining 2/3 strata: joint rows = 16
#>   after combining 3/3 strata: joint rows = 29
#> 
#> Exact conditional Poisson (categorical + STRATA; multivariate-shift algorithm)
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Parameter Estimate  StdError Alpha   LowerCL   UpperCL      PValue SuffStat
#>     group1 -1.26913 0.4605711  0.05 -2.372642 -0.335739 0.004763324        6
